title: The Missing Five Minutes: Practitioner Lessons from Building Code Calm as Postcrisis Recovery Infrastructure
abstract: High-intensity organizations often manage the beginning of a crisis more deliberately than its aftermath. Drawing on my experience developing Code Calm, a brief postevent practice for acute-care teams, this Practitioner's Corner reflects on recovery as an organizational design problem rather than an individual wellness task. Code Calm creates a voluntary five-to-seven-minute transition after difficult events through acknowledgment, grounding, somatic awareness, resourcing, and structured re-entry. The practice evolved through a pragmatic action-learning cycle of noticing, trying, reflecting, and redesigning. This process highlighted four design principles: protect the pause, preserve voluntariness, separate restoration from evaluation, and pair microrestoration with structural accountability. I conceptualize Code Calm as a microboundary practice: a protected interval between high-intensity action and routine re-entry. Its value lies not in promising rapid stress reduction, but in changing what organizations recognize as legitimate work and creating conditions in which recovery, sensemaking, and system learning can become possible after difficult work.
